newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Hoyts to spend A$47 mln in Sth America.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Hoyts to spend A$47 mln in Sth America.

text.p: Hoyts Cinemas Ltd said on Wednesday it planned to spend A$47 million on further expansion in Latin America over the next four to five years.
Hoyts Managing Director Peter Ivany, who earlier announced an expansion into Chile, also said the group expected to announce an expansion into another country later this calendar year.
Ivany said Hoyts was looking at another market in Latin America and had an office in Brussels where it was assessing its European strategy.
Ivany said Hoyts would invest about A$12 million in the Chilean expansion, but more funds would be pumped into the joint venture company to be set up to oversee its operations in Chile.
He said the joint venture partner in Chile, would be United Shopping Centres.
Hoyts plans to operate 42 cinema screens in Santiago during 1997.
He said Hoyts planned to open another 270 screens by the end of calendar 1997, bringing the total number of screens to be operated by the group to 1,400 by the end of the year.
Hoyts will have screens in Australia, New Zealand, United States, Mexico and Chile by the end of 1997.

Ivany said the funds spent on expansion would depend on how many countries Hoyts entered. "At the moment we have a plan to be in 10 markets over the next 10 years," he told reporters after the release of Hoyts first half results.

"A$500 million is what we orginally have indicated and after we went out to the market it got closer to A$600 million," said Ivany in reponse to a question on how much Hoyts will spend on expansion over the next five years.
Ivany said about 80 percent of the A$600 million is expected to be spent on its existing markets, mainly in the United States and Australia with the balance to be spent on new markets.
He said there was a lot of refurbishment work to be done in the United States market.
Hoyts reported a maiden net profit of A$12.17 million in the six months ended December 31, 1996. The cinema group listed on the Australia Stock Exchange in August 1996.
At 1.35 p.m. (0225 GMT), Hoyts shares were two cents lower at A$2.66.
